title: Model Interop Scorecard and Shadow Compatibility Radar
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: build a repeatable, quantitative scoring system that captures cross-model interoperability (API surface, prompt/format compatibility, quantization/precision mismatches, and embedding/semantic drift) and a live ‘shadow compatibility radar’ that surfaces imminent substitution risks for enterprise customers. This ticket scopes the PM work to define the rubric, run the first 12-model probe, synthesize procurement triggers, and wire alerts into the model-watch dashboard. Outputs: a CSV scorecard, an internal Confluence spec, a set of test prompts for probe harness, and an alert recipe for Console ops.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Scoring rubric defined with 6 dimensions (API compatibility, latency delta, output stability, embedding drift, quantization compatibility, enterprise contract friction). 2) Probe harness executed across 12 models with normalized scores in the CSV. 3) Confluence spec (link below) reviewed by Research and Engineering. 4) Alert recipe implemented in staging dashboard that flags models with >30% substitution risk. 5) Hand-off notes created for Solutions and Sales.
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Kickoff with Research, Eng, and Solutions; agreed on target dimensions and 12 candidate models (open-source + hosted).

decisions: Score normalization: use min-max per-dimension across the 12-model sample to start (decision made 2026-02-28).
Weighting: contract friction and embedding drift set to weight 1.5x other dimensions based on AE feedback (decision 2026-03-05).
Variant handling: quantized and fp16 variants run as separate rows in the scorecard; decision 2026-03-01.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: score overfitting to 12-model sample. Mitigation: schedule quarterly rebaseline and expand candidate set to 30 models next quarter.
Risk: probe harness may increase compute costs if run frequently. Mitigation: introduce sampling cadence and only run heavy probes on suspect models (cost cap enforced by Eng).
Risk: false positives from tokenization deltas causing noisy alerts. Mitigation: add debounce window and require >2 correlated dimensions to trigger a high-risk alert.
